meta_description: The estate as designed system — landing zones, network fabric and workload placement by economics.

blocks.x: The estate as designed system — landing zones, network fabric and workload placement by economics.

Multicloud sprawl is a cost decision nobody made. We design the estate as a system: landing zones per environment with policy-as-code guardrails, a network fabric (hub-spoke, private interconnect, egress control) that makes topology intentional, and workload placement driven by data gravity, latency, regulatory zone and unit economics — not by which team inherited which vendor relationship.

We are deliberately multi-vendor across AWS, Azure and GCP, and we write the placement policy down: a workload scoring model each team can apply, with review gates for exceptions. Sovereignty and sector constraints (data residency, regulated zones) are modeled as first-class placement inputs, so audits and architecture reviews read the same truth.
